identityReview: Li Qiang (李强), born July 1959, from Rui’an, Zhejiang; not predecessor Li Keqiang. Official educational distinctions retained. Wenzhou Party secretary from 2002, Zhejiang secretary-general from 2004, acting governor December 2012 and elected governor January 2013, Jiangsu and Shanghai Party secretary before national leadership. Politburo member in 2017, Standing Committee member October 2022, State Council premier March 2023. Current premiership confirmed by actual November 2026 meeting reports.
lifeStatusEvidence: Official speech and independent Reuters reporting document his actual attendance and remarks as premier at the 29th China–ASEAN leaders’ meeting in Manila on 16 November 2026. Scheduled later activities are not used as completed events.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read selected official biographies, provincial appointment announcements, CPC plenum communiqué, presidential order, contemporaneous news and Reuters profiles, HRW statement reproduced by ecoi.net, the short 2026 target report and substantive November speech. Read Commons crop/parent metadata and Council general copyright text; no image pixels or readable Newsroom-specific terms obtained.
corrections: Read the official March 2023 short biography. Use birth month only, native place rather than an independently verified birthplace, and distinguish postgraduate educational qualification from EMBA degree. This historical biography alone is not proof of a November 2026 current office.

Read the detailed career chronology. Agricultural mechanization study, management engineering coursework, Central Party School postgraduate qualification and Hong Kong Polytechnic University EMBA are different forms of study. Do not turn all of them into degree awards or duplicate master’s degrees. The October 25 URL contains a later Shanghai appointment in its updated text; use the separate October 29 announcement for that event.

Read the contemporary report of the provincial standing committee decision on 21 December 2012. Acting governor and vice-governor are not the subsequent elected governorship. Do not backdate the formal governor stage to all of 2012.

Read the January 30 contemporaneous report, including the session and election result. This supports the precise election date rather than relying on next-day republication dates. The adjoining Xia Baolong biography and doctorate belong to another person.

Read the June 30 Jiangsu announcement. It reports a central decision made recently and publicly announced at that day’s officials’ meeting. The timeline records the announcement meeting, without inventing the earlier date of the central decision or confusing later provincial Party elections with initial accession.

Read the October 29 Shanghai announcement. Separate city Party secretary from mayor and central Politburo membership from Standing Committee membership acquired later. The reported recent central decision and the date of its public announcement are not automatically identical.

Read the first-plenum communiqué and membership lists. The meeting occurred October 23; the ministry republication is October 24. The Party election does not appoint the State Council premier. Other officials named on the 2022 list are not assumed to retain their positions in 2026.

Read Presidential Order No. 1 dated 11 March 2023, following the NPC decision. The March 12 posting timestamp is not the appointment date. This is a state appointment, not a direct popular election; Li Qiang is not predecessor Li Keqiang or President Xi Jinping.

Read the Reuters career and appointment profile. Public text attributes the Tesla link rather than asserting sole personal responsibility. The description of his prospective influence is analysis, not proof that he subsequently strengthened the premiership. Education shorthand about master’s degrees is replaced with the official distinctions. Reports about lockdown and business ties are not criminal adjudications.

Read HRW’s April 2022 statement as reproduced by ecoi.net. It is an attributed human-rights organization’s account, not a court judgment against Li personally. Public text summarizes access to essentials; individual deaths, unverified social-media anecdotes and assumed personal orders are not added.

Read Reuters’ reporting on the Tesla letter and factory reopening. Company gratitude and local support do not establish Li personally arranged every operational measure, nor do they negate the wider impact of restrictions. Expansion plans in the letter are not treated as completed capacity.

Read the short Xinhua report on the March 2026 government-work-report targets. Growth is a range and a target, not a November observation or full-year outcome. Only the selected target extract was read, not the entire government report or an independent statistical audit.

Read the substantive speech sections identifying Li as premier and recording his November 16 Manila remarks. Cooperation proposals and future training or scholarship commitments are not completed results. His statements about trade and investment are not independently audited statistics; public text omits those totals.

Read Reuters’ current report confirming the November 16 meeting and his participation as premier. Future events mentioned elsewhere in the article are not evidence of completed attendance. This independently supports the current-role and recent-activity check; it does not verify every policy claim in the speech.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No birth certificate, original diploma, confidential decision record, complete government report, independent audit of speech statistics, original HRW case files, entire speech video or portrait pixels reviewed. Do not treat policy advocacy as achieved results, secondary predictions as established power changes, NGO criticism as a personal criminal verdict, or a Commons template as a substitute for source-specific permission.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons crop and parent description, metadata and history. Caption identifies the Kuala Lumpur meeting with European Council President Costa on 27 October 2025; timestamp is 03:40:22, not an independently validated camera clock. Crop 934×1207, 178 KB uploaded 26 November 2025 at 11:51; parent 4503×3000, 5.16 MB uploaded 25 November at 11:57, both by Sashi Suseshi. Commons labels Attribution and uses a European Commission template referring to Decision 2011/833, while the original is from the European Council/Council Newsroom. These institutions and legal policies cannot be silently equated. Read the Council’s general copyright rules: acknowledge source, preserve meaning, identify modifications, respect any specific and third-party restrictions. It directs readers to special Newsroom conditions; the item and About page expose no readable body, so image-specific permission remains unconfirmed. No stored portrait-cache fields in the raw evidence and no cache directory in this checkout. One original-image request on 18 November returned curl exit 22 with 403/HTTP 000, with no local file. No pixels inspected; identity, colour, framing, orientation and sharpness remain unreviewed.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields reviewed in seven foreign languages against Chinese and English. Preserve birth-month precision and native-place wording; coursework, Central Party School qualification and EMBA distinctions; acting/elected governor chronology; public announcement dates for Jiangsu and Shanghai; Party secretary versus mayor, Politburo versus Standing Committee, Party election versus state appointment; Li Qiang versus Li Keqiang; attributed lockdown criticism, multiple contributors to industrial projects, 2026 growth target versus achieved result, and actual November 16 meeting versus future proposals.
